text: RULING: NONE. The council should avoid all three IPO applications because the budget is too small for the listed minimums or the SME minimum is far higher. No candidate has sufficient evidence to expect better performance than the whole market by the 29-trading-day horizon. Weekly and monthly single-stock moves are mostly noise, while SME risks and lottery allotment are not compensated here. Any short-term listing gain would face the 20% short-term equity tax, with residency-dependent details; delivery and selling charges would also reduce returns. The 10x goal would take 29.9 years at 8% annually or 20.3 years at 12%, so no IPO is being rejected merely for failing to become a 10x in this month.
